claims.text: The investigated alloy has composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Melt spinning of this alloy achieves cooling rates of 10^5–10^6 K/s.
Slow cooling at approximately 52 K/s produces a complex multiphase crystalline microstructure in this alloy.
Very rapid melt-spinning cooling can produce an amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 ribbon.
The alloy forms several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases during solidification.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 undergoes a multistep crystallization sequence upon reheating.
A brief isothermal hold during DSC reheating at Tg < T_hold < Tx will suppress nucleation kinetics of the primary crystalline phases.
The isothermal hold allows atomic-scale structural relaxation without providing sufficient thermal energy for crystallite growth.
A temperature between Tg and Tx is below the energy threshold required for crystallization nucleation and growth during the hold.
Relaxation during the hold will kinetically trap the amorphous phase and delay or reduce non-eutectic crystallization.
Relative to continuous reheating, the hold will shift the crystallization exotherm to higher temperature.
Relative to continuous reheating, the hold will lower the intensity of the crystallization exotherm.
Samples receiving the hold will retain a higher amorphous fraction and have enhanced thermal stability.
Continuous reheating without a hold produces multiple crystallization exotherms.
The intervention is effective only when the hold temperature remains strictly between Tg and Tx.
The intervention should operate for samples prepared across cooling rates from approximately 52 K/s to above 10^5–10^6 K/s.
Cooling rate significantly changes the phase composition and transformation temperatures of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Phosphorus addition promotes amorphization and enhances glass-forming ability under rapid cooling.
High configurational entropy and heterogeneity in atomic size and bonding can disrupt crystal nucleation and slow grain growth.
XRD and TEM can distinguish the amorphous state from crystalline phases in the rapidly cooled alloy.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis applies an amorphous-retention intervention to slowly cooled samples described as already containing several primary crystalline phases. Reheating below Tx cannot by itself restore material that crystallized during cooling, so the predicted increased amorphous retention is not coherently bounded to samples that possess a measurable initial amorphous fraction.
